items.desc: DJ and curator Edna Martínez, from Cartagena de Indias, presents champeta, a genre born inside the picós, the sound systems of Colombia’s Caribbean coast where music is presence, tension, gathering. It carries fragmented routes shaped by circulation and bootlegs. It becomes body, dance, code, a way of occupying a space that has never been neutral. From the host: "For this Tierra Bomba Special, I bring together the champeta of Michel, Lilibeth and Edwin El Maestro. Three voices from the island, with songs from the mid-2000s to 2010. Stories of love, heartbreak, celebration and everyday life."

items.desc: Curator and DJ Edna Martinez explores the champeta, an underground musical genre and dance that originated in the Caribbean coast of Colombia in the early 1980s. The rhythms and influences are said to have arrived with the sailors from West Africa in the 1960s and 70s. We will get to know in each episode its specificities and the relevance of this scene. From the host: "A tribute to a legendary Cartagena picó El Parrandero since 1978, championing soca and Caribbean rhythms. The pure euphoria of Colombian caribbean sound system culture."
